marks.gloss_en: defense (c, final): the mishna's oath is rabbinic, so it does not bear on Sumchos's Torah-level rule
R' Yosei: where a swindler certainly exists, the whole disputed sum is impounded until Eliyahu comes, so the swindler loses
the Rabbis (two-depositors case): each takes the smaller sum; only the remainder is impounded until Eliyahu comes
(derived inside the hypothesis) per R' Yosei the garment should all the more be impounded, since it may belong wholly to one of them
the standing answer: there a swindler certainly exists; here perhaps both lifted it together and neither lies
alternative answer: R' Yosei impounds as a penalty to induce the swindler to confess -- pointless here where confession costs him nothing
storekeeper-and-laborer case: each swears and collects from the employer, though one certainly swears falsely
no impounding there: each litigant has an independent claim against the employer and is not bound by the other's oath
ותנא תונא: in the mishnah each side is backed by אנן סהדי on half, yet each swears on the rest -- as in statement I
two grasping a garment, each claiming all: each swears he owns no less than half, and they divide it
R' Chiyya (statement I): total denial met by witnesses attesting fifty -- he pays the fifty and swears on the remainder
Rabba: the presumption -- a person does not brazenly deny outright before his creditor
